name: ontology-manager
description: Manages ontologies for the Werkbank with OntoRAG (open source, Apache-2.0, pip: ontorag). Browse, search and compose baseline ontologies, register new ones, and query an ontology with its instances over SPARQL. Can also grow ontologies from documents: it reads documents, proposes new or extended ontology terms with the quotes they come from, and changes the catalog only after you confirm the reviewed proposal. Ships a small Finance Pre-Close baseline (company codes DE10, FR10, UK10, certified metrics such as Margin and DSO, pre-close checks). Runs on this computer through uv (needs uv; the first start downloads the OntoRAG packages). Reading and querying need no key. Proposing from documents needs a language model: the text of the documents is sent to the model endpoint you configure.

tools.name: list_ontologies
tools.description: List the baseline ontologies registered in the catalog.

tools.name: inspect_ontology
tools.description: Show the classes and properties of one registered baseline ontology.

tools.name: search_classes
tools.description: Search classes by name or description across all registered baselines.

tools.name: search_properties
tools.description: Search properties by name or description across all registered baselines.

tools.name: compose
tools.description: Merge selected baselines into one schema card with the origin of every term.

tools.name: add_ontology
tools.description: Register a new baseline ontology from Turtle (TTL) text. Adds to the catalog; nothing is overwritten by the connector itself.

tools.name: describe
tools.description: Describe one resource (class, metric, company code) by its IRI, as Turtle.

tools.name: list_by_class
tools.description: List the instances of a class, for example all company codes.

tools.name: outgoing
tools.description: Follow the relations that leave a resource.

tools.name: incoming
tools.description: Follow the relations that point to a resource.

tools.name: mentions
tools.description: Show where a resource is mentioned (provenance), when the instances carry mention nodes.

tools.name: sparql_select
tools.description: Run a read-only SPARQL SELECT over the ontology and its instances.

tools.name: sparql_construct
tools.description: Run a read-only SPARQL CONSTRUCT over the ontology and its instances.

tools.name: propose_ontology_from_documents
tools.description: Read documents or pasted text and propose a new ontology, or additions to an existing one, with the quotes each term comes from. Changes nothing in the catalog. Needs a model key; the text is sent to the model endpoint.

tools.name: list_ontology_proposals
tools.description: List the proposals made so far and their status.

tools.name: show_ontology_proposal
tools.description: Show the review report of one proposal again.

tools.name: apply_ontology_proposal
tools.description: Adopt a reviewed proposal, only with confirmed=true: register it as a new ontology or merge it into an existing one. The previous version is saved first.

tools.name: discard_ontology_proposal
tools.description: Delete one proposal's working files (confirmed=true). The catalog is not touched.

tools.name: document_ontology_settings
tools.description: Say whether a model is configured and which folders documents may come from.

ontology_folder.title: Ontology folder
ontology_folder.description: Absolute path of a folder on this computer where the ontology catalog is kept, for example /home/you/werkbank-ontologies. It is created if it does not exist. The bundled Finance Pre-Close baseline is registered there on the first start.

knowledge_ontology_file.title: Ontology file for queries (optional)
knowledge_ontology_file.description: Absolute path of a Turtle (.ttl) ontology that describe, list_by_class and the SPARQL tools read. Leave empty to use the bundled Finance Pre-Close baseline.

knowledge_instances_file.title: Instances file for queries (optional)
knowledge_instances_file.description: Absolute path of the Turtle (.ttl) file with the instances of that ontology. Leave empty to use the bundled sample instances. Set both files or neither.

documents_folder.title: Documents folder (optional)
documents_folder.description: Absolute path of a folder with the documents you want to turn into ontology proposals (.md, .txt, .html, .epub, .pdf). Only files below this folder and the connector's own inbox can be read. Leave empty to use pasted text only.

llm_api_key.title: Model API key (for documents)
llm_api_key.description: Key for the OpenAI-compatible model endpoint that proposes ontology terms from documents (OpenRouter by default). The text of your documents is sent to that provider. Not needed for a local server without a key requirement; stored as a secret, never written to config files.

llm_model.title: Model name (optional)
llm_model.description: Model the endpoint should use, for example openai/gpt-4o-mini. Leave empty for the OntoRAG default.

llm_base_url.title: Model endpoint (optional)
llm_base_url.description: Base URL of an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Leave empty for OpenRouter. For a model on this computer use its address, for example http://localhost:11434/v1.
